entries.text: The two of them stood in the warmth of the Hearth, the glow of the fire catching the quiet anticipation passing between them. Neither had to say much for the other to feel the pull of the unknown. Ash turned to Wren, the words hanging in the air between them—an unspoken question about the trader's strange treasure. Wren met the glance, sharing the same wondering thought before either of them voiced it. "A glowing stone from a cave no one remembers? That's worth a look. Let's go." Wren's eyes brightened at the thought, the story already taking shape. "A glowing stone from a cave he doesn't remember? That's the best kind of story. Let's go see it." With that, they moved together toward the door of the Hearth, stepping out into the night toward the Market's glow.

entries.title: At Hearth, the familiar warmth settles as the scene unfolds.
entries.text: At Hearth, the familiar warmth settles as the scene unfolds. Ash rises and heads toward the Market. Wren also moves toward the Market. Rollo lingers behind, observing the others as they depart. Rollo calls out to Wren: "Ah, Wren! Come see the glow I found—it's a sign of good fortune, I tell you!" Spotting Ash, Rollo adds: "Back again, eh? Care to see my glowing stone? I found it near that cave I can't remember—might be worth a look."

entries.text: Wren and Ash share a look at the Market, then both turn toward Rollo. Wren is the first to speak up, eager to see the trader's prize together. "Aye, let's have a look at this glowing stone together." "Ash, you beat me to it—mind if I look too? I've got a few questions for your trader about that cave." Rollo, standing by with the stone, waits for the two companions to come closer. Ash finally asks the trader directly. "You about done with that stone, Rollo? We came all this way for a look." "Certainly! Come closer and see the warm glow—strange, isn't it? I found it near a cave mouth I swear I've never entered. Could be old luck waiting to be claimed." "That's the spirit! Both of you, come have a look—it's a good omen, I swear by it."

entries.text: At the Market, a quiet pause settles over the three as Rollo stands, watchful, while Ash and Wren trade glances near the glowing stone. Ash moves first, trying to draw Wren's attention to the stone and to the cave it seems to hint at. Wren follows the thought, wondering aloud whether they should ask Rollo about that same cave. Rollo catches the unspoken question and answers it with a grin: "Ask away, Ash! The cave's a real curiosity—I'll tell you both all about it." Wren turns to Ash with a nod: "Good idea, Ash. Let's both step closer—I want to hear about that cave too, and see if the stone's glow is anything like the tales." Hesitating a step, Wren adds, "Ash, Rollo's just standing there—maybe he wants us to make the first move. Let's step closer and see the stone." Rollo gestures them nearer: "Wren, you and Ash have the right of it — step closer and see the glow for yourself. Ask away about that cave; I'll tell you all I remember, which isn't much, but it's a good omen all the same." Ash agrees quietly: "Aye, I'm curious about that cave too. Let's hear what Rollo says."

entries.text: The market buzzes around them, but Ash's attention is fixed on Rollo, pressing for answers about the cave and the stone's origin. Wren, too, edges toward the glowing stone, inviting Ash to step closer and question Rollo together. "Rollo, you're just standing there—let's see that stone up close. Tell us about the cave, then." Rollo answers Ash, "Happy to tell you both! The stone came from a cave I half-remember, but I swear I never walked in. The glow looks like good luck, and I'd be glad to lead you there if the price is right." Wren turns to Rollo, "Rollo, you said you'd tell us about the cave—I'm ready to hear it. And let's get a closer look at that stone while we're at it." Rollo beckons Wren closer, "Aye, step closer, Wren—see the warm glow for yourself! And I'll tell you both about that cave, such as I remember." "Aye, let's step closer. Rollo, show us that stone properly—and tell us about this cave you can't remember," Ash says, moving toward the glow. Rollo waits, letting the silence hang for a heartbeat before he speaks again.

entries.title: At the bustling market, the three exchange glances, each voice circling the same unspoken hope: the cave, the stone, and
entries.text: At the bustling market, the three exchange glances, each voice circling the same unspoken hope: the cave, the stone, and what they might be worth. Rollo's eyes light up as he turns to Ash, his voice carrying over the market noise. "Aye, Ash, you're speaking my language! Lead you to the cave? Gladly—if the price suits. Let's say ten silvers each, and I'll take you right to the mouth of it. The stone's glow is a good omen, I swear by it. What say you both?" Ash nods slowly, weighing the offer, then turns to Wren with a quiet certainty: "Aye, Wren, let's see that stone properly. Rollo's been keen enough—time to hear what he remembers." Wren steps forward, curiosity sharp in their voice as they address Rollo directly: "Rollo, I'm all ears about the cave—where is it, and what makes the stone glow like that?" Rollo beckons Wren closer, a grin spreading beneath his weathered beard. "Aye, come closer, Wren—let the glow catch your eye! And I'll spin you the tale of that cave, though parts of it are foggy as the morning mist." Wren glances back at Ash, pressing the matter in a low, determined voice: "Rollo, we're both eager to see that cave—tell us your price, and we'll decide together."

entries.title: At the bustling Market, the three companions huddled together as Wren turned to Ash, asking whether ten silvers each see
entries.text: At the bustling Market, the three companions huddled together as Wren turned to Ash, asking whether ten silvers each seemed fair and whether they should follow Rollo to the cave. "Ash, glad you're set on this. Then I'm with you—let's pay Rollo's ten and see that cave for ourselves." "Rollo, you mentioned ten silvers each. Before we agree, what exactly will we find at the cave mouth? I want a fair sense of what we're paying for." Rollo answered Wren's question about the cave's location and the stone's glow, explaining what he remembered. "Rollo, you said parts are foggy—but I still want to hear what you do remember. Where's the cave, and why does the stone glow? Ten silvers each sounds fair if it's real." "Ten silvers is a fair price, Wren—that cave's a good omen, and I'll make sure you both get there safe! What do you say, shall we go at dawn?" "Ten silvers each is steep, Wren, but if the cave's real and the stone's truly from it, might be worth it. Let's hear if Rollo can show proof or sweeten the deal before we hand over coin." "Aye, Ash, you've a good head on you! Ten silvers each it is—and I'll lead you straight to that cave. The stone's glow will guide us true, I promise you that."

entries.title: At the Market, the party gathers as Wren tries to catch Ash's eye, gesturing toward dawn.
entries.text: At the Market, the party gathers as Wren tries to catch Ash's eye, gesturing toward dawn. Rollo, in turn, presses Wren for details about the cave's location and the stone's mysterious glow. Ash holds back, waiting quietly as the others talk. "Ash, don't be shy—we're set for dawn! The stone's glow will lead us true, I swear it." "Go on, Rollo—where exactly is it, and what makes that stone glow? We're ready to hear the whole tale." "Aye, dawn it is. I'll have the coin ready—let's hold Rollo to his word." "Rollo, you still haven't told us where the cave is or why the stone glows. If you want our ten silvers each, give us a straight answer—not just promises." "Aye, dawn it is, Wren! I'll be ready with my cart and the stone's glow to light the way. Ten silvers each, and we'll see that cave before the sun's high."

entries.title: Wren pressed Rollo for the cave's location and the stone's glow secret before dawn, the urgency of the coming morning ha
entries.text: Wren pressed Rollo for the cave's location and the stone's glow secret before dawn, the urgency of the coming morning hanging in the market air. "Ash, while you're looking, what do you make of Rollo's story? I still half-expect the cave to be a burrow with a firefly stuck in it—but the stone does glow, and I'm curious enough to see it with my own eyes at dawn." "Ash, the cave's north of the vale, past the old oak with the split trunk. The stone glows because it's touched by the earth's own fire—lucky it is, and I swear it'll lead us true." Ash spoke to Wren, urging that they had pressed Rollo enough and that, given his evasiveness, they should hold him to specifics at dawn or walk away. "That's the first straight answer we've had. A half-day north past the oak—fair enough. But a cold glow like coal? I've never heard of such. I'll take your word for now, but I want to see that stone again before we set out. Dawn, then." Ash observed the pair in the market, weighing their words against the setting light. "Ash, he finally gave us a straight answer—the old oak by the stream, half a day north. A cold light, like a coal. That's more than promises. I say we take him up on it at dawn." "Wren, I've already told you—the cave lies east of the vale, half a day's walk, and the stone glows because it caught the moon's blessing. That's the whole tale, straight as I know it. Ten silvers each and we ride at dawn."

entries.title: At the market, Rollo sets the stone out where the dawn light can reach it, ready for Ash's inspection before they set ou
entries.text: At the market, Rollo sets the stone out where the dawn light can reach it, ready for Ash's inspection before they set out. Rollo calls over to Ash, "Aye, Ash, ten silvers each and the cave's a half-day north past the split oak—that's the bargain, and I'll show you the stone again before we set out." Wren gestures toward the stone and asks Ash, "Rollo's brought the stone out—shall we give it a proper look before we commit to the walk?" Ash tries to confirm with Rollo the price and the route before they leave—ten silvers each and the way to the cave. Wren turns to Ash and says, "Ash, good—let's lock in the ten silvers and the path. I'm ready to see that cave for myself." Wren stands by, waiting while the deal is settled.
